 Urban India’s festive spending likely to fall 6% to ₹1.97 lakh crore in 2026: Survey
 Urban consumers are prioritising clothing and fashion, while 83% of households planning festive purchases expect to use savings. Jewellery is among the least-preferred categories, with just 6% planning purchases. 
 By   Storyboard18 |  October 23, 2026, 18:28:01 IST Choose Storyboard18 on Follow Share Urban Indian households likely to spend ₹20,000 on festive purchases on average, down 6% from 2025
 ADVERTISEMENT
 Urban Indian households are expected to spend an average of ₹20,000 on discretionary purchases this festive season, with total spending projected to decline 6% from last year, according to a survey by LocalCircles. The estimate puts festive expenditure at ₹1.97 lakh crore in 2026, compared with ₹2.10 lakh crore in 2025. 
 The survey, which gathered more than 67,000 responses from urban consumers across 307 districts, found that 57% of households intend to make festive purchases. However, 31% do not plan to spend on discretionary items, while 12% remain uncertain about their budgets. 
 Among households planning to spend, 30% expect their outlay to fall between ₹10,000 and ₹1 lakh. Another 18% intend to keep expenditure below ₹10,000, while 9% anticipate spending more than ₹1 lakh. 
 The projected decline marks a reversal from 2025, when urban festive spending rose from ₹1.85 lakh crore in 2024 to ₹2.10 lakh crore. That increase coincided with GST rate cuts introduced in September last year.

 Clothing, footwear and accessories are the most popular planned purchases, with 72% of households intending to spend on these categories, the survey found. 
 Home appliances and furniture, along with travel and holidays, follow at 45% each. Gourmet food and gifting account for 39% of planned purchases. Mobile phones and consumer electronics and gadgets feature in the plans of 22% of households each, while another 22% intend to spend on home renovation and interiors. 
 Automobiles and two-wheelers feature in 10% of responses, while jewellery accounts for just 6%. 
 The survey findings also point to a greater reliance on existing funds to meet festive expenses. Among households planning discretionary purchases, 83% expect to use at least some savings to finance their spending. 
 About 34% plan to cover at least a quarter of their festive expenditure through savings. This includes 18% who expect savings to fund between 25% and 50% of their outlay, and 16% who intend to finance all their festive purchases from savings. 
 Meanwhile, 17% said they would rely entirely on their earnings rather than savings. No respondents selected borrowing as a means of funding their planned purchases. 
 Household spending outlook remains cautious 
 The survey comes amid rising prices and changing consumer sentiment. Retail inflation reached 5.54% in September 2026, up from 4.83% in August, while food inflation increased to 7.74% from 5.97%, according to government data cited in the survey. 
 The Reserve Bank of India raised the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50% on October 7. The central bank also increased its consumer price inflation forecast for FY27 to 5.2% from 5%, and expects inflation to reach 6% in the October-December quarter. 
 Consumer confidence indicators have also weakened. In the RBI's July 2026 Urban Consumer Confidence Survey, the Current Situation Index declined to 88.3 from 90.7, while the Future Expectations Index fell to 115.3 from 118.7. 
 Early festive sales data show a mixed picture. September GST collections increased 14.7% year-on-year to ₹2.04 lakh crore, while vehicle retail sales rose 31.8% to a record 25.37 lakh units. However, the Federation of Automobile Dealers Associations cautioned that the vehicle sales growth was partly influenced by a low base. 
 Online marketplaces have also reported strong activity. Flipkart recorded 6.3 million concurrent users, with around 60% of demand coming from non-metro customers. Meesho reported a 75% year-on-year increase in orders on the first day of its festive sale across fashion, beauty and festive décor. 
 Electronics demand could face greater pressure. Counterpoint Research expects festive smartphone volumes to decline 12% year-on-year as higher memory chip costs push up device prices, even as the market's value is projected to increase 5%.
